subject: Renewal usage & capacity — headroom scenarios for renewal decision
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluemap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal usage review + headroom scenarios

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time last month to walk through your migration plan. Attached is a short usage export and latency summary for BlueMap (Q4 2026) plus three compact headroom scenarios we modeled for the upcoming renewal. High-level notes: 

- Current monthly token consumption (rolling avg): ~120,000,000 tokens
- Recent 30-day 95th pctl latency on hosted endpoints: 420ms (peaks to ~780ms under sustained burst)
- Prefix cache hit rate on your most-used flows: 41% (we saw gains when you enabled longer session tokens)

The attached spreadsheet includes: baseline renewal (flat commit), +25% headroom, and +50% headroom with burst credits. My recommendation is to consider the +25% tier for predictable unit cost while enabling a small burst pool (one-time credits) for seasonal campaigns. That combo gives you ~20–25% headroom without doubling committed spend.

Can we set a 30-min slot this week to walk through the scenarios and map to pricing bands (and any performance targets you want to guarantee)?

Attachments: usage_report_q4-2026.csv, latency_summary_q4-2026.pdf

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluemap.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal usage review + headroom scenarios

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the export and the clear scenarios. A couple quick clarifying Qs before the call:

1) Can you break down the 120M tokens by environment? Rough split prod vs. staging vs. inference-batch? We need that to justify any committed uplift to finance.
2) That 95th pctl latency — how much of that is from large-context chat endpoints vs. smaller single-turn inference? If the large-context calls are the outlier, we might route those to a dedicated pool instead of increasing baseline commit.
3) On pricing: what is the uplift to per-token price at the +25% commit vs. +50% (line item)? Finance will want a delta per million tokens.

I can do Wednesday 10:00 PT for a 30-min sync. If you want to include a technical person from our side, I'll add Lina (our infra lead).

Best,
Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
BlueMap Systems
jordan.price@bluemap.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@bluemap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal usage review + headroom scenarios

Jordan —

Answers inline and attached a compact "uptick_budget_scenarios.xlsx" with the per-token deltas.

1) Token split (30-day window): Prod ~82%, Staging ~10%, Batch/async jobs ~8%. I included a small reconciliation sheet showing sample endpoints mapped to categories.

2) Latency breakdown: large-context chat endpoints (session lengths > 2k tokens) account for ~62% of high-latency tail events. Smaller single-turn calls average 250–320ms at 95th pctl. Given that, two practical levers look best:
   - Move large-context chat paths to a dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) to tighten latency SLA and reduce cross-tenant interference.
   - Keep interactive single-turn traffic on hosted with higher commit for unit-cost efficiency.

3) Pricing delta (excerpt from attached):
   - Baseline (flat renewal, no uplift): $0.95 per million tokens (effective blended rate after current discounts)
   - +25% commit uplift: $0.88 per million tokens (volume discount applied)
   - +50% commit uplift: $0.82 per million tokens

Operationally, the +25% commit + 30k burst credits scenario reduces expected overage exposure by ~48% while improving margin vs. pure pay-as-you-go. The Dedicated pool proposal has a fixed monthly platform fee + a lower per-million rate for the pinned endpoints — I put an example line in the spreadsheet to compare net economics.

I'll join Wednesday 10:00 PT; please invite Lina.

Attachments: uptick_budget_scenarios.xlsx

—Naomi

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal usage review + headroom scenarios

Team — forwarding BlueMap thread. Key asks from Jordan before Wednesday: token split validation and per-token delta. Can you please: 

- Karthik: confirm the Dedicated pool SKU economics for a 3-node T4/T4s-equivalent deploy (including platform fee) and a conservative 95th pctl latency target we can offer for large-context chat.
- Marissa: prepare a short finance-friendly delta table we can share at the call (current spend vs. +25% vs. +50% and expected monthly $ change). Also include simple payback window for the Dedicated pool if they move 30% of chat traffic there.

Quick context excerpted for your convenience:
> Jordan asked for split by environment and a line-item delta for +25% vs +50% commit.
> Large-context chat drives most of the 95th pctl latency tail; suggested Dedicated for those endpoints.

I'll be on the call Wednesday 10am PT and will lead the renewal scenarios discussion.

Thanks —
Naomi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal usage review + headroom scenarios

Thanks Naomi — I've sketched three quick SKUs and the likely latency SLOs; attaching those to the internal doc we're using. Bottom line: a 3-node Dedicated pool (mixed T4s, preemptible-capable) gets us comfortably under 300ms 95th pctl for the targeted large-context endpoints at their projected 30% traffic shift.

Marissa — I'll drop the SKU cost lines into your delta table. If we structure the renewal as a 12-month commit with a mid-year review and an optional auto-burst credit top-up, we can keep the effective blended price between the +25% and +50% bands and protect Redwood revenue against short-term surges.

Call Wednesday looks good — I'll be on to answer any technical or capacity questions.

-Karthik
